requirement: Work holding the heavy webroot lock runs at normal CPU priority, a queued Initial backup says it is waiting, and a demo site runs with a small Apache pool and small MariaDB buffers

oracle.ref: PR #1268 (fix); fix evidence: fleet01, 12/10/2026: ja-space held the heavy lock in 'building the webroot baseline' from 16:54Z to 17:40Z+ while ten installs waited; at 18:10Z 3.9 GB RAM, 32 MB available, 939 MB swap, load 18-22 on 2 cores, 184 apache2 (~3.4 GB) and 22 mariadbd (~2.3 GB). Lab (2 cores, real ja-space j6 webroot): baseline 2-3 s alone; beside 2 busy loops 6 s at nice 0, not done after 240 s at nice 19.
oracle.invariant: Every run exits 0 with 0 failures. No code line of webroot-git.sh, webroot-backup.sh or webroot-pack.sh (the three scripts that take the heavy lock) runs under nice. On Linux (taskset present): a baseline of 3000 files pinned to one core beside one busy normal-priority loop finishes in under 20 s (develop: killed at 30 s). An Initial backup queued behind a held heavy lock prints 'waiting for another site's webroot baseline', then 'taking the Initial backup (ADR 0024)' once it has the lock. A demo site's compose file mounts apache/tracy-demo-limits.conf (StartServers 1, MaxSpareServers 2, MaxRequestWorkers 6) and gives MariaDB --innodb-buffer-pool-size=16M --innodb-log-buffer-size=4M --aria-pagecache-buffer-size=8M --key-buffer-size=8M; a customer site gets none of them, and an install that is not a demo removes a leftover marker. tracy-host passes TRACY_DEMO_SITE=1 to provision.sh only for demo: true.
